newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Communist leaders tell Duma to pass Russian budget.
newsitem.headline: Communist leaders tell Duma to pass Russian budget.

text.p: The Russian Communist Party's top economic theorist called for the State Duma lower house of parliament to close ranks with the government and pass the 1997 draft budget in a first reading on Sunday.

"The style of work characterised by confrontation with the executive power does not take us anywhere. We need to change our style," said Yury Maslyukov, chairman of the Duma committee for economic policy. He called for the Duma to vote for the budget.
"Whether we want to recognise it or not, we have seen a correction to the course of reform towards investment growth."
Maslyukov's comment was a dramatic change from the communist line on December 6, the previous day of parliamentary budget debate, when party leaders called for the plan to be rejected.

But party leader Gennady Zyuganov told parliament that communists reserved the right to block the budget in later readings if certain conditions, such as an off-budget industrial investment programme and payment of back wages, were not met.
The draft has to pass three readings in the Duma before being submitted to the upper chamber, the Federation Council.
Communists and their allies are the largest bloc in the Duma.
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, who is to address parliament before it votes on the budget on Sunday afternoon, has promised to pay most government debts and create the investment fund.
Russian Finance Minister Alexander Livshits opened discussion of the 1997 draft budget on Sunday with a promise of money for regional administrations.

"We have managed to increase transfers to the regions by four trillion roubles ($720 million) in 1997," Livshits told the Duma, which has rejected the budget once and postponed a vote on the present draft to Sunday from December 6.
Livshits said the plan, on which a vote is expected at 1300 GMT, envisaged a deficit of 3.5 percent of gross domestic product.
